item.description:
Israeli military jeep runs over Palestinians in occupied West Bank

The Palestine Red Crescent Society said that two Palestinians were left wounded after being run over by an  Israeli military jeep near Jenin in the northern occupied West Bank.

The two were riding a motorcycle when the vehicle struck them. As a result, both victims suffered a broken foot, with one of them also sustaining a head injury.

item.title: IRGC says two oil tankers hit mines in the Hormuz Strait
item.description:
IRGC says two oil tankers hit mines in the Hormuz Strait

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said that two oil tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz, leading to explosions. 

The IRGC said in a statement that the vessels "attempted to pass through the illegal southern route and hit a naval mine with several very strong explosions, lighting up the sky of the Strait of Hormuz for hours".

"We warn the owners of oil companies that the southern American route created in the Strait of Hormuz is mined with fiery walls. Trusting the lies of the American military authorities and cooperating with them will make you a prey to fire."

China confirms meeting with Trump, Putin
item.description:
China confirms meeting with Trump, Putin

China has confirmed that President Xi Jinping and his US and Russian counterparts, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, are set to hold their first trilateral summit on Thursday in Shenzhen.

"On November 19, Chinese President Xi Jinping will hold a China-Russia-US heads of state meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen," the foreign ministry said.

The Kremlin and the White House have both previously confirmed the three-way meeting.

According to US officials, Trump wanted to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals as well as discuss the war on Iran. 

is also set to bring up his war in Iran -- but he is not expected to discuss Russia's war in Ukraine, US officials said.

Mossad abducted Iranian general in Turkey, tortured him for weeks before killing him: Report
item.description:
Mossad abducted Iranian general in Turkey, tortured him for weeks before killing him: Report

Israel kidnapped two Iranian officials and killed one of them in a decades-long search for an Israeli pilot whose fighter jet crashed in Lebanon while bombing the country in 1986, The New York Times reported on Sunday.

Israeli pilot Ron Arad was bombing Lebanese villages in 1986 when one of his missiles malfunctioned, forcing him to eject from his fighter jet.

Since then, Israel has been on a mission to find out what happened to Arad, leaving a trail of death and destruction in its wake which has left more than 40 people dead and dozens more wounded.

The NYT said that the search for Arad was rooted in the "Jewish tradition" to bring its soldiers back to Israel.

Read more: Mossad abducted Iranian general in Turkey, tortured him for weeks before killing him: Report

item.title: Israel, Taiwan pose threat to Somalia’s existence: Somali president
item.description: Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud announced Sunday that Israel and Taiwan pose a threat to Somalia’s existence, Anadolu reports. His remarks came during a speech at a ceremony marking the launch of construction of Somalia’s National Defense University in the capital, Mogadishu. “Taiwan poses a threat to Somalia’s existence, and Israel poses another threat to Somalia’s statehood. We know who our close friends are, and who are not,” Mohamud said during his speech at the launch of the university, which is also expected to include an armed forces hospital. China, which Mohamud said is one of Somalia’s closest allies, is funding the construction of the university. item.title: When the ladder collapses
item.description: A few days ago, Iraqi media carried the story of a young doctor loading sacks of cement at a construction site. He had completed medical school. He had done everything society had asked of him. He studied, graduated and acquired the qualifications his country desperately needs. Yet he could not find a job in medicine. What made the story striking was not simply that a doctor was working in construction. It was that a thread had snapped. item.title: Fire destroys Syrian refugee camp in Lebanon, leaving nearly 500 homeless
item.description: A fire swept through a Syrian refugee camp in eastern Lebanon on Saturday, destroying all 59 tents housing 75 families, witnesses said, Anadolu reports. The blaze broke out at the camp in Bar Elias, a town in the Zahle district of the Bekaa Valley, where about 486 people were living, an Anadolu correspondent reported. The fire destroyed the entire camp, leaving hundreds of Syrian refugees without shelter. No injuries were reported, and Lebanese authorities had not commented on the cause of the blaze. Lebanon has hosted large numbers of Syrian refugees since the conflict in Syria began in 2011. Lebanese authorities estimated the Syrian refugee population at about 1.5 million in January, including nearly 880,000 registered with the UN refugee […]

item.title: US intel estimates Iran retains up to 2,500 missiles despite war damage: Report
item.description: Iran retains an estimated 1,500 to 2,500 missiles despite months of US and Israeli strikes targeting its weapons infrastructure, the Wall Street Journal reported Sunday, citing US intelligence assessments, Anadolu reports. The findings challenge US President Donald Trump’s claims that Tehran’s military capabilities have been largely destroyed. Citing US officials, the newspaper said the assessment suggests Iran still possesses a substantial missile arsenal capable of threatening American and allied targets if fighting resumes. Officials said the assessment carried a low level of confidence because of difficulties determining how many missiles were ready for launch and how many remained in storage.
